# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment

The incumbent uses 12 LUTs and 4 FFs, passes simulation, and fails setup timing at WNS −0.753 ns while hold passes at WHS 0.109 ns. The reported critical path runs from `read_ptr` through distributed RAM selection to `out_data[7]`; the top has known latency 1, so its `// @latency 1` annotation must remain.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the dynamically indexed two-entry storage with explicit front and back data registers will drive `out_data` directly from a register, removing the read-pointer-to-LUTRAM output path and potentially recovering setup timing, at the cost of additional FFs.

## Instruction for generator

In `skid_buffer_core`, replace `storage[0:1]` and `read_ptr`-based output selection with an explicit front register that drives `out_data` and a back register for the second queued word; update them on accepted pushes and retired pops, including simultaneous transfers. Preserve the two-entry occupancy rules, combinational `in_ready`, synchronous active-high reset priority, stall stability, one-cycle minimum transfer age, and full throughput; data while `out_valid` is low remains unspecified. Keep the top interface and `// @latency 1` unchanged, then judge the candidate using the frozen simulation and routed setup, hold, and utilization gates.
